findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Place the s3:// helper preflight guard at the shared store-mount/init engine seam (the *_core mount path) rather than only in `_commands/init.py`, so MCP and library-facade init also fail closed with the actionable message per AC-2.
evidence: 'wire that guard into src/rebar/_store/push.py and src/rebar/_commands/init.py so s3:// remotes fail closed when the helper is missing/old'
AC-2: 'store init and push fail closed'
Bypassing ingress paths: MCP server (src/rebar/mcp_server.py) and library facades that mount/init a store without invoking the _commands/init.py CLI handler
findings.finding: AC-2 requires 'store init ... fail closed' when the helper is missing/old, but the Preflight-enforcement child wires the init-time guard only into the CLI command `src/rebar/_commands/init.py`. The MCP server and library-facade init/mount ingress paths do not necessarily route through that CLI module, so the init-time fail-closed check is placed on one interface surface. The push-time guard in `_store/push.py` (shared seam) still fires for all surfaces, so this is a scoped concern about the init-time half of AC-2, not the push half.
findings.location: Child decomposition → Preflight enforcement: 'wire that guard into src/rebar/_store/push.py and src/rebar/_commands/init.py'
scenarios: A library consumer or MCP-driven init/mount of an s3:// store bypasses the CLI-only init.py guard, so the actionable pip-install message never fires at init time (the failure only surfaces later at push).
If a store-mount library facade exists, it initializes an s3:// remote with a missing helper without the fail-closed message AC-2 promises for the init step.
findings.suggested_fix: Identify the shared mount/init core function that CLI, MCP, and library facades all call, and invoke require_s3_helper() there; keep _commands/init.py to CLI-only message formatting.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the S3 bucket configuration reproducible/idempotent and drift-resistant — provide a declarative form (e.g. a small Terraform/CloudFormation snippet or an idempotent script) for the SSE-KMS default encryption, versioning, and public-access-block, and state how drift on the default-encryption setting is detected/re-asserted.
evidence: "put-bucket-encryption ... ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault ... aws:kms"
"At-rest encryption therefore comes from the bucket's default encryption ... it is not optional hardening."
The commands are imperative shell (`aws s3api create-bucket ...`), not declarative/idempotent IaC; no mention of drift or re-application safety.
findings.finding: The durable bucket configuration is delivered as imperative `aws s3api` one-shot commands (create-bucket, put-bucket-encryption, put-public-access-block, put-bucket-versioning) with no idempotency or drift handling; because at-rest encryption depends ENTIRELY on the bucket's DEFAULT SSE-KMS setting (the doc's own load-bearing warning: the helper does not request per-object SSE), out-of-band removal of that default silently un-encrypts all new ticket history with no detection.
findings.location: docs/s3-backend.md §2 'Create the bucket (SSE-KMS) and the IAM policy'; AC-4
scenarios: An operator or another tool removes/edits the bucket default-encryption or public-access-block out-of-band; nothing re-asserts it and new ticket bundles land unencrypted or public-reachable.
Re-running the documented `create-bucket` on an existing bucket errors, leaving operators unsure the config converged.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Document recommended observability for the ticket-store bucket (S3 server-access logging or CloudTrail S3 data events, plus any bucket monitoring) so mutations — including auto-doctor bundle deletes — are auditable.
evidence: ABSENCE: neither the plan nor docs/s3-backend.md mentions S3 access logging, CloudTrail data events, or any alarm/metric on the bucket.
The auto-doctor deletes bundle objects (§5), a mutation worth auditing.
findings.finding: The plan provisions no observability for the ticket-store bucket: there is no S3 server-access logging, CloudTrail data-event capture, or bucket-level monitoring/alerting for the object mutations rebar's auto-doctor performs (bundle writes + deletes), so an unexpected multi-bundle heal or an unauthorized access has no audit trail.
findings.location: docs/s3-backend.md (all sections); plan 'Child decomposition' — Docs + ADR
scenarios: Ticket history is unexpectedly rewritten or a bundle disappears; the operator has no log to reconstruct who/what mutated the bucket.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the merge strategy the auto-doctor uses (e.g. a merge commit uniting all divergent heads as parents so all events remain reachable, with a defined conflict-resolution rule).
evidence: 'merges all divergent heads under a repo-level repair lock and collapses them to one bundle'
'every commit/event from all divergent heads is reachable from the healed tip'
No stated merge strategy (e.g. merge commit uniting parents, -X ours/theirs, or event-log union) is given.
findings.finding: AC-3 requires the auto-doctor to 'merge all divergent heads' with 'every commit/event from all divergent heads reachable from the healed tip', but the merge conflict-resolution semantics are unspecified — for a git merge of two divergent orphan-branch heads, how conflicting bundle/tree contents resolve is left to the executor.
scenarios: Two heads modify the same ticket file; a plain git merge conflicts and the non-interactive heal has no defined resolution, stalling or aborting.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify that the heal creates an octopus/sequential merge commit whose parents are all divergent heads (union of history), guaranteeing reachability regardless of tree conflicts.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the Auto-doctor's conflict-handling contract in AC-3: how a genuine content conflict between divergent heads is detected and surfaced (fail-loud with an actionable operator message) so the lossless/no-discard guarantee is well-defined for the merge's failure case.
evidence: AC-3: 'merges all divergent heads under a repo-level repair lock and collapses them to one bundle' and 'every commit/event from all divergent heads is reachable from the healed tip (no head or event discarded)'

The plan names no merge driver or conflict policy for the ticket data format, yet a lossless merge of two heads is only guaranteed when files do not truly conflict (ABSENCE rationale: failure-case of the core mechanism is unspecified in plan text)
findings.finding: The merge-heal mechanism (AC-3 / Auto-doctor child) does not specify the FAILURE case: what happens when two divergent heads carry a genuine content conflict that a plain merge cannot resolve losslessly. AC-3 asserts full reachability from a single merged tip but is silent on conflict handling, which is the merge mechanism's key failure edge.
scenarios: Two divergent heads modify the same non-UUID/shared file (e.g. a store-level state file) so the fold hits a real conflict — the plan does not say whether the heal errors loudly, escalates, or how the operator recovers

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Cite the exact git-remote-s3 release (changelog/PR) that introduced the IfNoneMatch per-ref lock and confirm it matches the `>=0.3.2` pin the fail-closed guard depends on.
evidence: Plan: 'declare the optional `[s3]` extra (`git-remote-s3>=0.3.2`)'
Plan AC-2: 'absent or below the pinned minimum ... fail closed'

awslabs/git-remote-s3 README (retrieved): 'This locking mechanism eliminates the race conditions that could previously result in multiple bundles per reference' — confirms the lock exists but not the introducing version
This is an unverified capability assertion ('helper >=0.3.2 has the IfNoneMatch lock') that the whole fail-closed guard rests on
findings.finding: The plan pins `git-remote-s3>=0.3.2` and makes fail-closed behavior depend on being 'below the pinned minimum' (AC-2), asserting 0.3.2 is the version with the IfNoneMatch per-ref lock, but does not cite which release actually introduced that lock. Retrieved upstream docs confirm the locking mechanism exists ('eliminates the race conditions that could previously result in multiple bundles per reference') but the plan does not resolve the exact version boundary the pin encodes.
scenarios: A helper version >=0.3.2 that predates the lock passes the guard yet still creates multi-bundle state
The pin is set too high and rejects a working helper

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the ADR, briefly record the encrypted-git-remote backends considered and rejected (e.g., git-annex S3 special remote) and why git-remote-s3 was chosen, so the backend decision is grounded in prior art rather than a single experiment.
evidence: Plan evaluates only `git-s3 doctor` as prior art for the heal; the backend decision is asserted from a single live experiment
Retrieved HN thread (news.ycombinator.com/item?id=41887004): 'Git-annex can use any of its special remotes as git remotes, like what the presented tool does for just S3' — a named comparable backend
ADR child owns 'record the architecture decision (git-remote-s3 backend ...)' but the plan text gives no alternatives-considered for the backend
findings.finding: The plan justifies the merge-based auto-doctor against the ONE alternative it evaluated (upstream's interactive `git-s3 doctor`) but does not record any consideration of alternative encrypted-git-remote backends before committing to git-remote-s3 — e.g., git-annex special remotes, which the retrieved HN discussion raises as a comparable approach for using S3 as a git remote. The anti-repackaging check on the backend choice itself (not just the doctor) is unstated.
findings.location: Context / Problem; Child decomposition: Docs + ADR (records the architecture decision)
scenarios: A reviewer of the ADR asks why git-remote-s3 over git-annex or a plain atomic-CAS object-store helper and finds no recorded comparison

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the Auto-doctor (merge-heal) child, name the exact git-remote-s3 private-API surface the heal depends on (bundle enumeration, per-ref repair-lock acquire/release, raw bundle write+delete) and state it was verified against the pinned git-remote-s3>=0.3.2 (cite the observed symbols/signatures at the pinned commit), or route that surface through a short SPIKE before committing the heal build.
evidence: Plan: 'a new non-interactive self-heal that ... merges all divergent heads under a repo-level repair lock and collapses them to one bundle. Owns: the healing mechanism.'

Context proves only init/create/claim/push/fetch + non-FF recovery via the experiment; the multi-bundle heal is described as a risk to 'own', not a verified capability: 'Upstream's git-s3 doctor repairs it but is interactive-only ... Not usable for an autonomous agent fleet.'

Collapsing bundles requires reusing the helper's undocumented per-ref lock and raw object writes/deletes — an internal API surface distinct from the git-remote helper protocol the experiment exercised.

Evidence class = Unverified for the heal surface: resolve_symbol('git_remote_s3') returned UNRESOLVED (optional [s3] extra not installed), so the private symbols cannot be confirmed from this environment; NOT proof of absence, but the plan supplies no verification of its own.
findings.finding: The Auto-doctor (merge-heal) child asserts a new capability — non-interactively enumerate a ref's bundles, take the helper's per-ref repair lock, and write/delete raw bundle objects to collapse them to one — that depends on git-remote-s3 PRIVATE internals, but the plan text neither names those internals (e.g. bundle enumeration, per-ref lock acquire/release, raw object write/delete) nor states they exist and were verified at the pinned git-remote-s3>=0.3.2. The live experiment proved the git-layer path (init/create/claim/push/fetch + non-FF recovery) but only ISOLATED the multi-bundle risk; the heal mechanism itself was not exercised in the proven experiment.
findings.location: Child decomposition — 'Auto-doctor (merge-heal)'; also Context bullet 'Multiple-bundles corruption'
scenarios: If git-remote-s3 v0.3.2 exposes the per-ref lock / bundle enumeration / object delete only through a shape the plan assumes (names, signatures, key layout) but that differs, the auto-doctor fails to collapse bundles — leaving the store unclonable, the exact hard-fail AC-3 promises to fix.
A minor upstream release changes a private symbol and the heal breaks silently despite the >=0.3.2 pin admitting future versions.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to the Auto-doctor child listing the verified private symbols at v0.3.2 (e.g. S3Remote, parse_git_url, acquire_lock/release_lock, get_bundles_for_ref, init_remote_head) with the observed source location/commit, and tighten the pin to a bounded range (>=0.3.2,<0.4) since the heal binds to undocumented internals; note AC-3's real-git-repo test exercises this surface via the injected S3Remote factory.
